newsitem.title: USA: TWA machinists threaten airline with suit. [CORRECTED 00:48 GMT 4/2]
newsitem.headline: TWA machinists threaten airline with suit. [CORRECTED 00:48 GMT 4/2]

text.p: The International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers on Monday warned the board of Trans World Airways Inc that it may file a court action if the directors move forward with proposals the union believes "run afoul of their fiduciary duties."

In a prepared statement, the union said it would "be left with no other alternative but to file a court action" unless the board agreed to take no further action to shrink the airline through asset sales, closings or layoffs, pending consideration of a purchase, merger or strategic alliance.

In a related move, the union, which represents more than 15,000 TWA employees, unanimously voted "no confidence" in the current interim Chief Executive Officer Gerald Gitner. (Corrects spelling of surname from Ginter to Gitner.)
In a prepared response, Gitner said he was "dismayed" by the union's stance and the positions taken in the original letter, saying that "it seriously misstates the plans and intentions" for TWA.
TWA spokesman John McDonald added that the union has always been fully aware of management's plans.
"The union is on the company's board," he said. "These actions are being taken by a board on which the union sits."
Gitner's letter to William O'Driscoll, president of the Air Transport District Lodge 142, said the company's current strategy was "not to shrink TWA and certainly not to allow TWA to fail."
The letter did not directly address the "no confidence" vote or the call for Gitner to step down in 60 days or less.

In another prepared statement, William Scheri, general vice president of transportation for the union, said, "The answer here is a restructuring with new management, not further asset sales and massive layoffs of IAM members, flight attendants and pilots."
